turns.user: Compare the free tiers of Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare Pages for a small side project.
turns.answer:
Cloudflare Pages is the most relaxed for a side project. Vercel and Netlify both pause or block you when you hit a cap, and they work quite differently. Figures are as of 11 Nov 2026.

| | Vercel Hobby | Netlify Free (new accounts) | Cloudflare Pages Free |
|---|---|---|---|
| Usage cap | 100 GB Fast Data Transfer, 1M function invocations | 300 credits/month, hard limit | Unlimited requests on a purely static project |
| Builds/deploys | 100 deployments per day | Production deploys cost 15 credits each; previews are free | 500 builds/month, 1 at a time |
| Commercial use | Non-commercial only | Commercial allowed (from the older Free plan announcement) | Not covered in the pages I found |
| Notable limits | Static uploads capped at 100 MB (CLI) | 1 concurrent build | 20,000 files per site; 25 MiB max file size |
| If you exceed it | You can't buy extra usage | Sites pause until the next cycle, and one project over its limit pauses all your projects | Functions requests hit a daily cap if you add Functions |

Netlify's 300 credits go fast. Bandwidth costs 20 credits per GB and web requests cost 2 credits per 10,000, so a busy site could exhaust them well before Vercel's 100 GB would run out.

Cloudflare's own docs now say Workers supports most Pages use cases, and new projects should start with Workers.

**Pick:** Cloudflare for static sites with real traffic, Vercel for Next.js (non-commercial only), Netlify for light use or forms.

log.answer:
**Neon is the cheapest for a small app.** It's free to start, and light paid usage costs a few dollars a month. Supabase jumps to $25/month once you need a paid plan. I couldn't pull a current RDS instance rate, so that row is a gap.

| Supabase | $0, 500 MB database, but free projects pause after 1 week of inactivity | Pro starts at $25/month. It includes $10 in compute credits, which cover one Micro instance. |

- **Neon** scales to zero after 5 minutes idle, so an app with sporadic traffic costs very little.

log.user: Does Neon still have a free plan, and what are its main limits?
log.answer:
Yes, Neon still has a free plan. It has no monthly cost, and it has no time limit and needs no credit card. These are its main limits, per Neon's docs and FAQ (last updated 3 Nov 2026):

- **Projects:** 100 projects, with 10 branches each.
- **Compute:** 100 CU-hours per project per month. Compute scales up to 2 CU (about 8 GB RAM) and scales to zero after 5 minutes idle.
- **Storage:** 1 GB per project, up to 20 GB across all projects.
- **Network transfer:** 5 GB per project per month.
- **Restore history:** 6 hours, capped at 1 GB of change history.

The limits are hard cutoffs. If you use up the CU-hours or network transfer, compute suspends until the next billing period or until you upgrade. If a project goes over 1 GB, writes that add storage fail, and Neon doesn't bill overages on Free.

Some older articles still quote 0.5 GB per project and 20 projects. Those figures are out of date. As of November 2026, the Free plan has 100 projects, each with 100 CU-hours and 1 GB.

**Neon is the cheapest managed option for a 10 GB Postgres, and Supabase is the one to pick if you also want login and file storage built in.** Prices below are as of 11 Nov 2026, in USD per month.

| Provider | Rough cost for ~10 GB | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Neon (Launch) | Typical spend is about $15 for a small database | No fixed monthly fee. Compute pauses when idle, and storage is $0.35/GB-month. |
| Supabase (Pro) | $25 base plan, with 8 GB of disk included, then $0.125 per GB | Includes $10 of compute credit, enough for one Micro instance. The free plan caps the database at 500 MB. |
| Render | $19 for a 1 GB RAM instance plus $3 for 10 GB of storage | Storage is $0.30/GB-month. Backups are point-in-time recovery, with a 3-day window. |

Neon's cost is usage-based, so it can rise with traffic. Supabase and Render are closer to flat monthly fees. If your app already runs on Render, keeping the database in the same workspace and region avoids egress charges.

Avoid free tiers for anything real. Render's free Postgres expires after 30 days, with a 14-day grace period before deletion.
